column1: # boru Language Specification: the boru:array-util module
# Loadable module of APL-style array utilities. Import binds the
# `ArrayUtil` namespace, then words are called via dot-access:
# words (iota/range/take/shed/each/fold/...) stay in core; this module

column3: shape: the length along each axis (2 rows, 3 cols)
rank: the number of axes
reshape: lay flat data into the given shape
transpose: swap rows and columns of a rank-2 list

column1: import "boru:array-util"  ArrayUtil.where [true false true false true]
column3: where: indices of the truthy elements
grade: indices that would sort the list ascending
at: select data elements by an index list
replicate: repeat each element by its count
expand: spread data into true slots, 0 into false slots
compress: keep data where the mask is true

column1: # §2b editing — copy-returning single-element edits (HAMT Level A primitives)

column3: insert-at: insert the element before index 1
insert-at: index 0 prepends
insert-at: index == length appends
insert-at: pipeline form (subject from the stack)

column1: import "boru:array-util"  def xs [1 2 3] end def ys (ArrayUtil.insert-at 1 99 xs) end xs
column3: insert-at is copy-returning — the source list is unchanged
insert-at: index past length is a loud error, not a silent no-op
insert-at: negative index is a loud error
remove-at: drop the element at index 1
remove-at: index 0 drops the head
remove-at: pipeline form (subject from the stack)
remove-at: index == length is a loud error
remove-at: any index into an empty list is a loud error
member: is each needle present in the haystack
unique: distinct elements, first-seen order
indices: position of each needle in the haystack, -1 if absent
group (1-arg): map each key to the indices where it occurs

column1: # the membership/grouping words compare by deq — the VALUE equality
# (NUR015 fix: they previously keyed on the rendered form, a third
# equality notion): scalars by value (eq and deq coincide there),
# Nodes/Ideals by deep value (eq is reference identity there).
# group is the exception, and deliberately so: its keys are STRINGS ONLY
# (NUR030, resolved 2026-08-15). A Map key IS a string, so a non-String
# key had to be RENDERED, and two deq-distinct keys that rendered alike
# then shared one entry. Restricting the domain removes the lossy step
# instead of judging it benign — the collision cannot arise. The map key
# is the string's CONTENT, so a group's own output is readable back with
# the key the caller supplied; it previously was not (the key carried the
# render's quote characters, and `get 'a'` on the result returned None).

column3: cross-leaf magnitude dedups: 1 deq 1.0
structurally-equal lists dedup, though eq (reference) distinguishes them
NaN is deq-unequal to itself — both kept, honestly

column1: import "boru:array-util"  def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1]  def g fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1]  size (ArrayUtil.unique [f/v g/v])
column3: NUR031: the deq scan merges two deq-equal FUNCTIONS — DeqKey buckets a function by its canon, matching deq's content equality

column1: import "boru:array-util"  def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1]  def h fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 2]  size (ArrayUtil.unique [f/v h/v])
column3: …and keeps two whose bodies differ, exactly as deq answers
membership by value: 1.0 is in [1 2]
…and by deep value for Nodes
index lookup by value
group (2-arg): bucket values by their parallel key
the key the caller supplied reads the group back — the map key is the string's CONTENT
…and the key set is exactly the supplied keys, carrying no render quoting

column1: import "boru:array-util"  def S (refine String) end def k:S 'a' end ArrayUtil.group [k 'a'] [1 2]
column3: a refined String is deq to its plain twin and groups with it, under the shared content key

column1: # The two NUR030 folds, now DECLINED rather than folded. Both rows flipped
# 2026-08-15 with the fix: the first was the deq-distinct collision that
# opened the record, the second the non-reflexive key it also absorbed.

column3: a type literal and a same-named atom no longer collide — neither can be a key at all (NUR030)
NaN is FORBIDDEN as a key rather than folded; was {nan:[1 2]} (NUR030)
the 1-arg form loses generality by design — convert first (NUR030)
the 2-arg form declines a non-String key too
none is not a String either
a single bad key in an otherwise-String list is declined
window: all contiguous slices of the given width
pairs: consecutive overlapping 2-tuples
eachrank: apply a body at cell-rank 0 (each scalar leaf)
eachrank at cell-rank 1: the body sees each INNERMOST LIST, not its scalars — the cell type is rank-dependent, which is why the compiled body takes a gradual carrier
foldaxis 0: reduce down each column
foldaxis 1: reduce along each row

foldaxis over an EMPTY rank-2 list: no lane to reduce, so the result is empty — and the body's input carrier has no element to take a type from, which is the gradual-Any arm of the compiled body's shape

column1: # Mixed-type ROWS (2026-09-02, found in review of the analysing ReturnsFn): a
# lane draws its elements from EVERY row, so the body's carrier is the join
# over all rows' elements. Typing it from the first row alone baked an
# Integer overload into the compiled body — `[3 0]` where the interpreter
# answers `[3 'ab']` — and, once the ReturnsFn analysed the body, into the
# result's consumers too. Rectangular means equal LENGTH, not equal type.

column3: mixed rows, axis 1: the body meets an Integer lane and a String lane
a heterogeneous row: the carrier is a Disjunct the body distributes over, not the Scalar ancestor
an operand-starved body over the statically-empty list is never run, so it is never analysed (scan's guard)
one row, zero columns, axis 0: no lane at all
one row, zero columns, axis 1: one EMPTY lane — nothing seeds the accumulator (was a lane[0] panic)
